what_it_does: When a phone runs low on RAM, it compresses less-used app data and keeps it in a special region of RAM called ZRAM rather than ejecting the app entirely. The problem is that when you reopen that app, the phone must decompress everything on the spot, causing a slow and CPU-hungry relaunch. Ariadne fixes this by sorting the compressed data into hot, warm, and cold buckets based on which parts the app actually touches first at relaunch. Hot data is compressed in small chunks so it decompresses fast; cold data is compressed in large chunks for space efficiency. A third trick starts decompressing the next expected chunks before the app even asks for them, so the CPU and decompressor can work in parallel and the user sees a faster launch.
